intent: The alert's own headline - a short label for what the alert is about.
typical_uses: The first line inside an Alert, naming the message before its longer description

dont_use_when.situation: A heading anywhere outside of an Alert

instead.note: AlertTitle carries Alert's own typography and the icon-column layout hook; Heading puts a heading on the type ramp anywhere else.

invariants.text: When the enclosing Alert has a direct <svg> child, AlertTitle is the part pushed into the icon layout's second column; AlertDescription is not, because grid auto-placement already skips the icon's row-spanning cell for it.
Without `render` AlertTitle is a div. With `render={<h3 />}` (any heading level) the element changes and the title class stays, with the UA heading margins and font reset at zero specificity.

anti_patterns.dont: Put the alert's leading icon inside AlertTitle
anti_patterns.do_instead: Render the <svg> as a direct child of Alert, before AlertTitle - the icon layout is detected off Alert's direct <svg> children, not AlertTitle's

render.states: render replaces the rendered div with an element the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (AlertTitle passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the heading element, such as `render={<h3 />}`.

good.title: A short headline above the alert's description
good.code:
<Alert>
  <AlertTitle>Update available</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>A new version is ready to install.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>

bad.title: Leading icon nested inside AlertTitle
bad.why: The icon layout is detected off Alert's direct <svg> children, not AlertTitle's; an icon nested here renders inline with the heading text instead of switching to the icon column.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered div with an element the caller supplies. useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (AlertTitle passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the heading element, such as `render={<h3 />}`.
